meta.title: Patient Engagement Software: What It Does and Why
meta.description: What patient engagement software does, which features drive results, how it differs from a patient portal, and how to choose a platform for your clinic.

hero.h1: Patient Engagement Software: What It Does and How to Choose a Platform
hero.subhead: A patient portal gives people a place to log in. Engagement software gives them a reason to act. Here's what separates the two, and how to evaluate a platform for your clinic.

content.body:
Patient engagement software helps a clinic communicate with patients and get them to take the next step in their care, before, during, and after a visit. That includes completing intake, confirming appointments, messaging the care team, reporting symptoms, and answering surveys.

The term covers a wide range of products, from a simple text reminder tool to a full [patient app](/features/patient-app). So before comparing vendors, get specific about which actions you want patients to take more often, and what each one is worth to your practice.

content.h2: Patient Engagement Software vs a Patient Portal
content.body:
A portal is largely passive. It holds records and messages, and it works when a patient remembers to log in, finds their password, and knows what to look for.

Engagement software is active. It reaches out at the right moment, usually with a link or a push notification, and asks for one clear action. The practical differences show up in a few places:

• **Who starts the interaction:** Portals wait for the patient. Engagement tools prompt them.
• **How much effort it takes:** Good engagement flows take a tap or two, with no login hurdle at every step.
• **What happens next:** A response should update your workflow automatically, rather than sit in an inbox.

Many clinics need both. The real question is whether patients are completing the actions your clinic depends on.

**Pre-visit intake and check-in**
This is often the quickest win. When patients finish forms and consent before they arrive, [digital check-in](/features/check-in) shortens the front desk line and improves data quality. Completion rate is the number to watch, as we explain in our guide to [check-in completion rates](/blog/check-in-completion-rates).

**Two-way reminders and rescheduling**
A reminder should let the patient confirm or change the appointment on the spot. Otherwise, it often turns into a phone call or a [no-show](/blog/no-show-reduction-scheduling).

**Secure messaging**
[HIPAA-compliant messaging](/features/secure-messaging) can take routine questions off the phones and give patients a direct line to the care team. Find out how messages are routed, and what the rules are for responding.

**Real-time updates during the visit**
Long, unexplained waits are one of the most common sources of frustration. Showing patients where they stand, through tools like [LobbyView](/features/lobbyview), helps set expectations.

**Between-visit monitoring**
For chronic conditions, patients can report symptoms and adherence between appointments. In some cases, this can support [remote therapeutic monitoring](/features/rtm), a billable service. Our guide to [RTM enrollment](/blog/rtm-enrollment-participation) covers how to get patients to participate.

**Feedback collection**
[Post-visit surveys](/features/patient-satisfaction) give you timely feedback and a chance to reach an unhappy patient before they leave a public review.

content.h2: How to Evaluate a Patient Engagement Platform
content.body:
Run every vendor through the same questions:

1. **Does it integrate with our EHR?** Ask what data flows in each direction. If staff have to re-enter patient responses, you've added work.
2. **What does the patient have to do?** Try the flow yourself on your phone, from the first text message to the finished task. Count the taps, and note every login and download.
3. **Does it work for all our patients?** Check languages, accessibility, and options for patients who don't use smartphones. If you serve many older adults, see our article on [self-service check-in for elderly patients](/blog/self-service-check-in-elderly-patients).
4. **What happens to the response?** Each action should trigger something: an updated chart, a staff task, or a change in status.
5. **Is it secure?** Ask for the business associate agreement and details about how patient data is protected.
6. **What does it really cost?** Ask about per-message fees, add-on modules, and implementation.

Ask each vendor for adoption and completion figures from clinics like yours, and how those numbers were measured.

Logins and downloads are easy to count, but they don't tell you much. Measure the actions tied to your operations:

• Intake completion before arrival
• Appointment confirmation rate
• No-show rate, by visit type
• Inbound phone calls per visit
• Message response time
• Survey response rate
• Monitoring participation, if you run an RTM program

Set a baseline before rollout, and review the results with your front desk team. They'll often know why a number moved before the report does.

content.h2: Why Adoption Usually Comes Down to Workflow
content.body:
A strong platform can still fail if patients never hear about it. Adoption often depends on small operational choices: who introduces the tool, when the first message goes out, and whether staff can help patients finish a task on the spot.

Start with one workflow, usually pre-visit intake, and make it work well before you add another. Give your front desk a short script. Track completion by location and provider, and find out what the best-performing teams are doing differently. Our article on [front desk burnout](/blog/front-desk-burnout) explains why this work pays off for staff as well as patients.

faqs.question: What is patient engagement software?
faqs.answer: It's software that helps clinics communicate with patients and prompt them to take actions like completing intake, confirming appointments, messaging the care team, and reporting symptoms.

faqs.question: What's the difference between a patient portal and patient engagement software?
faqs.answer: A portal mainly waits for patients to log in and find information. Engagement software reaches out at the right moment and asks for a specific action, then feeds the response into the clinic's workflow.

faqs.question: What features should a patient engagement platform have?
faqs.answer: Look for pre-visit intake, two-way reminders, secure messaging, real-time visit updates, between-visit monitoring, feedback surveys, and EHR integration.

faqs.question: How do you measure patient engagement?
faqs.answer: Measure actions tied to operations, such as intake completion, appointment confirmations, no-show rates, call volume, and survey response rates, rather than logins or downloads alone.

faqs.question: Is patient engagement software HIPAA compliant?
faqs.answer: It depends on the vendor and how the product is used. Ask for a business associate agreement and details on how patient data is secured.
